questions.prompt: What is the difference between a .gltf and a .glb file?
options: A .glb packs the JSON, binary data and textures into one file; a .gltf keeps them in separate files
A .glb is a 2D picture of the model
explanations: Correct: same glTF data, but .glb is one binary file: one path, one download.
Both hold real 3D data. Neither is a picture.
glTF supports animations in both forms.
They are the same format (glTF 2.0) packaged differently.

questions.prompt: Which file format is designed for 3D on the web?
explanations: .fbx is common in game and animation tools, but heavy and not built for the web.
.obj is old and simple: no animations, materials in a separate file.
Correct: glTF is often called "the JPEG of 3D".
.psd is a Photoshop image, not a 3D model.

questions.prompt: Where do you import GLTFLoader from?
explanations: Correct: it's an add-on, so your import map also needs a "three/addons/" entry.
GLTFLoader isn't in the main three.module.js file; it's an add-on.
There's no package called 'gltf' in your import map.
Browsers don't understand glTF on their own; Three.js's loader reads it.
questions.hint: It's an add-on, not part of the core.

questions.prompt: In loader.load(path, onLoad), which object do you add to the scene?
explanations: gltf is a plain object holding the results; adding it gives "object not an instance of THREE.Object3D".
Correct: gltf.scene is the 3D model (a Group).
Those are animation clips, played with an AnimationMixer.
The loader downloads the file. It isn't a 3D object.
questions.hint: The results object has a property that is the model itself.

questions.prompt: Spot the bug. The console says: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rotation').
options: Line 6 runs before the model has finished loading
explanations: Correct: loading happens in the background, so line 6 runs while model is still undefined. Move it inside the callback.
gltf.scene is right; gltf isn't a 3D object.
const can't be reassigned later, so line 3 would break.
A wrong path gives a 404 in onError, not this error.

questions.prompt: Your page is index.html, your code is in js/bg.js and your model is assets/robot.glb. Which path do you pass to loader.load()?
explanations: That's relative to bg.js, but the browser resolves paths against the page.
Correct: relative to index.html, which sits next to the assets folder.
The model isn't inside js/, and a leading slash breaks on GitHub Pages project sites.
That's a path on your own computer; visitors can't reach it.
questions.hint: Paths are relative to the page.

questions.prompt: The model loads on your Windows laptop but is a 404 on GitHub Pages. The file is Robot.glb and the code loads 'assets/robot.glb'. Why?
options: GitHub Pages is case-sensitive: Robot.glb and robot.glb are different files
The model is too big for GitHub
GitHub Pages needs a leading slash
explanations: Correct: Windows ignores capitals, the web doesn't. Match the name exactly.
GitHub Pages serves .glb files like any other file.
Size would make it slow, not a 404.
A leading slash would point outside your project site.

questions.prompt: You double-click index.html and the model won't load (a CORS error in the console). What's the fix?
options: Open the page through a local server, e.g. VS Code's Live Server
Move the model into the js folder
explanations: Correct: browsers block loading files from file:// pages. A local server serves them over http.
The format isn't the problem; file:// is.
Lights don't affect whether the file can be downloaded.
The folder doesn't matter; the browser blocks file:// loads anywhere.
questions.hint: Look at the address bar: file://…

questions.prompt: Which line makes the model twice as big in every direction?
explanations: Correct: the same as model.scale.set(2, 2, 2).
That moves the model; its size doesn't change.
That turns it by 2 radians (about 115°).
Three.js objects have no size property; use scale.

questions.prompt: You want to turn the model to face the other way (180°). Which line is correct?
explanations: Rotation is in radians: 180 radians is about 28.6 full turns.
Correct: π radians = 180°. (Or THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(180).)
Turning around x flips it upside down.
That moves it up by 3.14 units.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order to play the model's Wave animation.
explanations: Create the mixer for the model, find the clip, start its action, then update the mixer every frame so the animation moves.
questions.hint: Each line uses something the one before it created.

questions.prompt: Which line in your animation loop spins the model on its Y axis, the same speed on every screen?
explanations: Correct: it adds a little every frame, scaled by delta time, and waits for the model to load.
That sets one fixed angle, so the model stops instead of spinning.
That moves it upward, forever.
That stretches it taller every frame.
questions.hint: Add to the rotation every frame, scaled by delta.
